Ingredion Incorporated, through its wholly owned subsidiary Prospect Sub, Inc.
Strategic (global manufacturer and supplier of starch and sweetener ingredients, p. 1)

$19.00 per share in cash, without interest; options cashed out at the spread over exercise price. No financing condition; Ingredion to fund from available cash and revolving credit borrowings (pp. 2–3, 45).
10/15/2014, press releases before the opening of trading

In 2007 and 2009 two industry parties made unsolicited indications of interest; Penford signed a confidentiality agreement with each and exchanged information, but neither made an offer. Dated only to the year, so they get no rows (p. 23).
Met (process 1): 4 parties (Ingredion, Party C, Party D, Party A)

facts.field: Currency and units of bid prices
facts.value: US dollars per share of Penford common stock, generally stated on a fully diluted basis

Ingredion approached Penford’s CEO in July 2014 while activist shareholder SEACOR was running a director slate. It bid $17.00 orally and then $18.00 in writing in August. Penford declined exclusivity and gave Ingredion a management presentation, a dataroom and site visits to push its price up. Deutsche Bank’s September market check contacted six strategic companies; Parties A, C and D signed NDAs and B, E and F dropped away. Ingredion rose to $18.25–$18.50 and then $19.00 after Penford asked for at least $20.00, and on 10/03 the board moved to definitive negotiation with Ingredion. Party D withdrew, Party A bid only $16.00, and Penford signed with Ingredion at $19.00 cash on 10/14/2014.

cells.Question: Are Ingredion’s early price references bids? On 07/19 Fortnum said $16.00 would be a challenge. On 08/06 he said $17.00 “could likely get support”. On 09/29 the board called $16.00 Ingredion’s “initial indication”.
cells.Recommended answer: Record 08/06 as an informal $17.00 Bid: Ingredion said it was ready to propose, and Penford answered it as a proposed price. Keep 07/19 as a valuation statement: no offer was made, and the $16.00 is the 52-week high.

cells.Why, with page: P. 28 (six in early–mid September); p. 29 (F contacted 09/24); p. 32 (total of six: two declined NDAs, one no reply, three remaining).
cells.What changes if answered differently: If the September six excluded F, there were seven contacts, including one unnamed Strategic contact that never entered. Add one Contact row; entries, the auction screen and live counts would be unchanged.

cells.Question: Should Ingredion’s round-1 bids be Formal? Ingredion sent its own draft merger agreement on 09/06, before its 09/17 and 10/02 price moves, and sent a markup on 10/08.
cells.Recommended answer: Keep them Informal. The 09/06 draft came with no price and was not expressly tied to a proposal (E11 test 1). Formality is recorded at the 10/14 reaffirmation.

cells.What changes if answered differently: If Formal, Ingredion’s last three priced rows become Formal (Conditions Unclear), and the 10/14 row loses its purpose as a reaffirmation.

cells.Question: Is the 10/14 confirmation of $19.00 a Bid reaffirmed (Formal)?
cells.Recommended answer: Yes. Ingredion itself confirmed its standing $19.00 price while the agreement was being finalized with it, after weaker draft financials had raised a repricing risk. Its latest priced row (#37) is Informal.
cells.Why, with page: P. 32: Fortnum called “to confirm the proposed price of $19.00”; the board was told the price “remained at $19.00”.

cells.Question: Party C’s exit: Not selected at signing (inferred) or an earlier drop or withdrawal?
cells.Recommended answer: Keep inferred Not selected at signing by 10/14. The filing never reports C withdrawing or being excluded, and the market check stayed open after 10/03 (A was pursued; D met Deutsche Bank on 10/08).
